thread:
ashwin: Heads up — saw a ~25% p95 increase on mixtral-prod after last night's runtime kernel heuristics tweak. Happening across 3 regions. anyone seen this?

maria: saw a spike in tok/sec latency graphs, looks correlated with new kernel picker change. grabbing profiles now. :mag:

chris: which models are affected? mixtral only or qwen too?

ashwin: mostly mixtral-8x and qwen-6b when requests include the new chat template (system + user + assistant markers). embeddings unaffected.

elaine: quick dump from the perf agent — kernel selection fallback to byte-fallback path for inputs with special tokens. snippet:```
[INFO] model=mixtral-8x kernel=byte_fallback reason=tokenizer_mismatch prefix_len=32
[DEBUG] kv_cache_misaligned=true suggested_kv_stride=64 actual_stride=31
```

maria: oh that kv_cache_misaligned flag is new — looks like the tokenizer produced a different BOS/EOS handling for system messages, which shifts the stream and knocks the kv cache alignment heuristic.

chris: any evidence batching heuristics also changed? we pushed a conservative coalescing tweak yesterday. Could that increase head churn and cause more kernel switches?

ashwin: yes: profiler shows frequent kernel rebinds mid-request when batch includes mixed chat templates. p99 shows extra memcpy + kernel-swap cost ~6-8ms per swap.

perf-bot: perf-alert: mixtral-8x p95 latency increased 24% (12:30 UTC), traced to runtime commit abc123.

elaine: repro script I ran locally: two requests, one with system token wrapper and one without. when mixed in same batch runtime chooses different kernel for each and triggers fallback layer. logs:```
--- request A (sys wrapper) ---
tokenizer: byte_fallback path
kernel: generic_byte_kernel
kv_stride: 31
--- request B (no wrapper) ---
tokenizer: rope_path
kernel: rope_optimized_kernel
kv_stride: 32
```

maria: so the tokenizer decision (byte vs rope) toggles kernel and kv_stride. That should not happen mid-batch — batching heuristics should coerce compatible kernel variants or split the batch. looks like a bug in the kernel compatibility comparator.

chris: I can reproduce with a minimal harness. attaching command:```
curl -X POST https://mixtral-test/serve -d '{"prompt": "<|system|>You are a concise assistant<|end|>\nUser: hi"}'
```
Run two requests in same batch and you'll see swap.

ashwin: mitigation idea: make tokenizer decision deterministic at request enqueue time and annotate request with kernel_hint so batcher groups by kernel_hint. cheap patch while we fix comparator.

elaine: also need to check RoPE scaling path — when kernel picks rope_optimized_kernel but RoPE scaling is toggled for long sequences we sometimes fall back to generic kernels because scaled-rotary math isn't supported by the chosen kernel. that interplays badly with the tokenizer mismatch.

maria: agreed. short-term: 1) disable the kernel picker change (revert abc123) 2) add kernel_hint tag at enqueue 3) add extra unit test for mixed-chat-template batches. would cut p95 back quickly.

chris: I'm on the revert PR now. will add tests. anyone want to own adding kernel_hint?

ashwin: I can add kernel_hint to the enqueue path, will keep it opt-in behind a flag.

perf-bot: deploy-bot noticed a canary of abc123 last night. pausing broader rollout.

elaine: follow-up: we should also update tokenizer integration tests to include system markers and ensure BOS/EOS normalization doesn't create off-by-one tokenization shifts. small change in tokenizer plugin cascades into kv alignment, batching, and kernel selection.

maria: logging action items: revert runtime commit (chris), kernel_hint patch (ashwin), tokenizer normalization tests (elaine), add batcher compatibility test for mixed kernel types (chris+ashwin). I'll open tracking ticket. :white_check_mark:

ashwin: thanks — I'll push the patch with the flag and a short note in the rollback PR.

chris: PR up: r/7429 revert abc123, running canary now.

maria: monitoring dashboards look better after canary roll back, p95 trending down. will keep an eye for a full rollback confirmation.

perf-bot: perf-alert resolved: p95 returned to baseline after revert.

elaine: after this stabilizes we should schedule a deeper audit of kernel compatibility matrix (ropecore vs byte-fallback vs quant kernels) and add an end-to-end perf test that includes chat templates + special tokens.

ashwin: agreed. thanks team — nice triage and quick revert.
